content:
Alex: FYI customer ACME reported a p99 jump on /v1/generate starting ~03:00 UTC — dashboard shows ~1200ms but the raw histogram widget still shows >95% of requests <200ms. Filing ticket #4567 but want quick sync.
Meera: saw the alert too (obs-bot). Can you paste the dashboard query? my first thought is a bucket boundary change or a bad rollup job.
Alex: ticket link: https://redwood/support/4567
Alex: dashboard query (from the panel):
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```
But the rollup panel uses a precomputed p99 rollup metric from our aggregator (rollup.request_latency.p99)
Samir: obs-bot alert: "ALERT p99_latency_v1_generate > 1s for 5m" — looks legit. I ran a quick scrape of raw buckets and noticed a spike in the `+Inf` bucket coming from host-34 in us-west-2.
Devon: traced a few request IDs in the ticket, one shows a backend model cold-start where KV cache miss cascaded into a long tail: trace_id=trace-0a1b2c. Host-34 had ~40 slow tails in that window.
Meera: that would explain raw histogram vs rollup mismatch: rollup aggregates across hosts and time windows differently (we currently take per-host p99 then max across hosts for SLA). The histogram panel is global aggregated buckets -> quantile, so a small number of high tail events on a single host can inflate the per-host max but not the global bucket quantile the same way.
Alex: ok that matches. Is host-34 noisy due to infra changes? we rolled a kernel update to that ASG at 02:50 — could be related.
Samir: repro steps I used locally: run `wrk -t4 -c200 -d60s http://api.internal/v1/generate` with payload that hits large seq lengths. I also ran this PromQL to exclude host-34 and the p99 drops back to ~180ms:
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_ms_bucket{host!="host-34"}[5m])) by (le))
```
So sounds like isolated host noise.
Devon: mitigation proposals: 1) reroute ACME traffic off host-34 (temporary), 2) add host-level suppression to the alert for a short incident window, 3) backfill a derived panel that uses global quantile over aggregated buckets so dashboards are comparable.
Meera: agree. Also we should avoid using "max of per-host p99" as customer-facing SLA calc — it's what triggered the escalation but is confusing when raw histogram disagrees. I'll open a doc to standardize p99 derivation.
Samir: I've applied a quick route to dedicated pool for ACME (ACME-DEDICATED-01) and created PR to change alert query to ignore single-host spikes: https://github.com/redwood/observability/pull/987
support-bot: Ticket #4567 updated: rerouted to dedicated capacity, host-34 isolated from rolling pool. Customer notified, monitoring for 30m.
Alex: thanks. Follow-ups: ops to check kernel rollouts on host-34 ASG, infra to investigate KV cache cold-start increase, product to consider model fallback for big seqs. We'll reconvene if p99 doesn't normalize by 04:15 UTC.
Meera: noted :thumbsup:
Samir: will watch the p99 panel and post updates if anything else pops up.
